open_points.subject: canonical_values.content_identity sorting of order-free lists
open_points.text: Lists whose order carries no meaning are sorted before hashing — ports by (`direction`, `name`), nodes by `node_id`, edges in the edge order of A05, constants by (`to_node`, `to_port`)
open_points.question: How are items ordered when the stated sorting keys are equal, especially multiple edges with the same endpoints or multiple constants targeting the same port, so that identity remains independent of submission order?
options: Preserve submission order for tied items
Break ties using each item's full canonical bytes
Refuse every duplicate sorting key before identity is computed
open_points.default_guess: Break ties using each item's full canonical bytes.

open_points.subject: ordering of embedded collections returned by read operations
open_points.text: Every collection in an output is in store order unless the operation names another order.
open_points.question: What order must be used for embedded value collections whose members have no individual store positions, such as ports, nodes, edges, guards and constants returned by `read_contract_version`, `read_binding` and `read_flow_version`?
options: Preserve the order stored from the first submission
Use the canonical sorting orders used for identity
Define a separate order for each embedded collection
open_points.default_guess: Use the canonical sorting orders used for identity.

open_points.subject: installation.current_token_list after a failed configuration re-read
open_points.text: Re-read when the file's digest changed or it cannot be read; the four checks only; a failed re-read leaves no list until one passes
open_points.question: After a readable but invalid re-read clears the token list, which digest is remembered and when is the unchanged file tried again, including when the owner restores bytes identical to the last valid configuration?
options: Retry on every request while no valid token list exists
Remember the invalid file's digest and retry only after its bytes change
Keep the last valid digest and retry whenever the current digest differs from it
open_points.default_guess: Retry on every request while no valid token list exists.

open_points.subject: bindings.check_installed_instances manifest validation
open_points.text: an unreadable record, or one failing a check of the record itself (A08 rule 5), fails at its service
open_points.question: Which exact A08 rule 5 checks are “checks of the record itself” at startup when this operation has no operation name or proposed ports, and must it validate every capability or only the top-level record and selected instance facts it reads?
options: Validate only top-level parsing, service identity, capability-name uniqueness and the selected instance facts needed for header collision checks
Validate every capability entry using all checks that do not require proposed ports
Apply the complete proposal validation to some designated operation
open_points.default_guess: Validate only the top-level record and selected instance facts needed by the startup check.

open_points.subject: flows.compose_flow_version constant schema
open_points.text: A constant's StoredValue takes the `value_schema` and class the composing agent declared with it ... so a version whose constant targets a missing port, or one whose stored schema is not the declared one, is still kept and fails its proof
open_points.question: Can a kept constant's StoredValue schema differ from the constant's declared schema, or does “stored schema” here mean the target port's stored schema?
options: The StoredValue schema always equals the constant's declared schema; the intended comparison is with the target port's stored schema
The StoredValue may carry a schema different from the declared schema
Such a mismatch is a composition refusal
open_points.default_guess: Treat “stored schema” as the target port's stored schema; the constant's StoredValue uses its declared schema.
